title: VSZAPOWER Compliance Center
description: Model-specific VSZAPOWER charger test reports, standards and document requests for rechargeable coin cells.
lead: Match your VSZAPOWER product to its tested design, report number and scope. Documentation for one model or version does not automatically cover another.
search: Search by model or report number
noResults: No matching report. Check the model or request documents below.
batteryText: For LIR2032, LIR2016, LIR2025, LIR2450 and ML2032, specify nominal voltage, capacity, product version and destination market. The team must confirm document availability and scope for the selected version.
batterySafety: ML2032 requires its own charging specification. Do not assume an LIR charging profile is suitable. Standard CR primary cells must not be recharged.
scope: Results apply to the submitted sample, tested materials and listed methods. They are not blanket certification for every product or market. Transport documentation also depends on the battery, packaging and shipment configuration.
questions: Why are there two VZ002 entries?
Does an EMC report cover every CE requirement?
Does RoHS mean zero restricted substances?
Can battery and charger reports be combined?
answers: VZ002 identifies two different designs, with separate report sets. Match the product photo and report number.
No. It addresses the tests and standards listed in the report. A Verification of Conformity is not an EU Declaration of Conformity.

Request documents using the form. Access depends on the intended use, privacy requirements and reproduction conditions.
Each report stays linked to its tested object. A charger report does not cover every battery bundle; a battery transport report does not establish charger compliance.
formIntro: Specify the model, version, destination market and intended use so we can identify the relevant documents.
privacy: Your business contact information is used to respond to this enquiry.
success: Your request was saved. Our team will review the model and document scope.
